text.autoconfig.YungsRoads-fabric-1_21.o: Valid Structures
List of structures that can act as endpoints for roads.
Each entry can be a structure ID or a structure tag.
Must be a comma-separated list, encased in square brackets.
Example: "[#minecraft:village,minecraft:shipwreck_beached]
Node Step Distance
The distance between adjacent pathfinding nodes, in blocks.
Lower values follow the terrain more closely, but are slower to generate.
Jitter Amount
The maximum noise-based sideways offset applied to the road's shape, in blocks.
Heuristic Weight
How strongly pathfinding is pulled toward the destination. 1.0 always finds the cheapest road.
Higher values generate faster but give slightly less optimal roads.
Slope Weight
The extra cost of steep terrain. Each step's cost is multiplied by (1 + Slope Weight * grade^2).
Higher values make roads avoid hills and mountains more.
Max Grade
The steepest rise over run allowed between two nodes. Steeper terrain is never crossed.
1.0 is a 45 degree slope.
Water Weight
The extra cost of bridging water. Each bridge's cost multiplier is increased by this amount.
Higher values make roads detour further to avoid rivers and lakes, or to find a shorter crossing.
Max Bridge Length
The longest bridge a road may build, in blocks.
Roads cross rivers and lakes only on straight bridges, so wider water must be routed around.
0 disables bridges. Oceans are never crossed.
Smoothing Radius
How far along the road its height is averaged, in blocks.
Higher values give gentler slopes, with more cutting and filling to level the ground. 0 follows the terrain.
Max Cut Depth
The deepest a road may cut into the ground above it to stay level, in blocks.
Where the ground rises higher, the road rises too.
Max Fill Depth
The deepest gap under a road that's filled with ground, in blocks.
Deeper gaps, such as ravines and cave openings, are crossed on a land bridge instead.
Max Land Bridge Length
The longest dip in the terrain that a road crosses on a land bridge, in blocks, if it's deeper than Max Fill Depth.
Longer dips are followed instead.
Ravines and caves made by carvers always get a land bridge, since routing can't see them.
Land Bridge Edge Roughness
How ragged the edges of land bridges are, from 0 to 1. 0 gives straight edges.
Higher values move each edge block up to a block in or out.
Land Bridge Decay
How much of each land bridge's deck is missing, for a ruined look, from 0 to 1.
Blocks are likelier to be missing toward the edges, and the center line is always kept.
0 keeps the whole deck.
Extra F3 Info
Show the structure region and road node at your position on the F3 screen.
Place Roads
Whether to place road blocks.
Raw Node Markers
Place purple wool towers at each road node's position before jitter.
Jittered Node Markers
Place redstone block towers at each road node's final position.
Endpoint Markers
Place emerald block towers at each road's endpoints.
Straight Debug Lines
Place gold block lines straight between each road's endpoints.
Debug Paths
Place single-block diamond paths instead of normal roads.
